Mesa Business Strategy Lab problem statement

Vobiz.ai: Building an International Go-to-Market Engine

About Vobiz.ai

Vobiz.ai is an AI-native telephony infrastructure platform with pre-call intelligence, powering Voice AI agents, conversational AI and programmable enterprise communications globally. It provides the communications layer that lets businesses, AI platforms and developers make, receive and manage voice calls at scale, with a focus on low latency, call quality, reliability and intelligent call delivery. Its core capabilities include:

  • Programmable telephony: SIP trunking, Voice APIs, global phone numbers, real-time audio streaming and call controls
  • Pre-call intelligence: number health and reputation monitoring, spam-label detection and caller identity management to improve answer rates
  • AI-optimised connectivity and observability: low-latency, single-hop routing, HD voice, and real-time call quality monitoring
  • Global reach and integrations: phone numbers in 130+ countries, and compatibility with Voice AI platforms such as Vapi, Retell AI, ElevenLabs, LiveKit, Pipecat and OpenAI Realtime

The Context

Vobiz sits where telephony infrastructure, Voice AI and intelligence meet, helping enterprises and AI builders improve the performance, reach and scale of their voice applications. Its international infrastructure is already in place. The next step is commercial: growing customer adoption, channel partnerships and distribution across the Middle East, Europe and Southeast Asia.

The Problem Statement

How can Vobiz.ai build a scalable, repeatable and revenue-generating GTM engine across the Middle East, Europe and Southeast Asia? The team will answer five commercial questions:

  • Where to enter first: which countries and customer segments offer the strongest near-term revenue opportunity?
  • Who to sell to: which companies have immediate or emerging demand for programmable telephony and Voice AI infrastructure?
  • Who can sell with Vobiz: which channel partners, AI platforms, system integrators and technology partners can speed up adoption?
  • How to acquire customers: which outbound, ecosystem, developer and partnership channels can generate qualified opportunities?
  • How to turn this into revenue: what is the practical 90-day plan to generate meetings, pilots, proposals and production customers?

Scope of Work

  • Market prioritisation: evaluate countries on market demand, Voice AI adoption, competition, ease of selling and availability of partners
  • Customer prospecting: identify direct customers across Voice AI platforms, enterprises, CCaaS and UCaaS providers and other relevant segments, along with key decision-makers. Build a qualified database of 150–200 target accounts per region
  • Channel partnerships: identify resellers, system integrators, Voice AI platforms, telecom aggregators and technology partners for referrals, integrations and co-GTM. Shortlist 30–50 partners per region
  • Competitor intelligence: analyse global and regional competitors, including Twilio, Plivo, Telnyx, Vonage and local CPaaS and telecom providers, covering positioning, pricing benchmarks and differentiation
  • GTM channel discovery: test acquisition channels such as targeted outbound, developer communities, industry events, technology marketplaces, associations and ecosystem partnerships, and recommend the best ones with clear execution plans
  • Outreach and market validation: write tailored outreach, start approved conversations with customers and partners, validate interest, qualify opportunities and set up introductory meetings

Expected Output

  • A market prioritisation of countries and segments across the three regions
  • A qualified pipeline: 150–200 target accounts and 30–50 partners per region, with decision-makers and early conversations
  • A competitive positioning and pricing benchmark against global and regional players
  • A 60–90 day GTM playbook for each region, covering target segments, positioning, channels, partnership strategy, outreach plans, KPIs and priorities

The team will be measured on research quality and real GTM progress, such as qualified conversations and meetings set up, not just the number of names collected.

Deliverables so far

  • Solution deck (17 slides)
  • Insight document
  • Progress summary
  • Vobiz GTM Solution PDF (5 pages) and the Southeast Asia partner database and leads spreadsheets (files from the chat)

Step 1

Product understanding

Vobiz is a one-year-old Bengaluru startup that sells the phone-line layer underneath voice AI agents. It is strong in India and has close to no proven traction abroad.

Company snapshot

ItemDetail
Legal entitiesilaimitado Private Limited (India) and Vobiz, Inc. (Delaware, US)
Founded2025, Bengaluru; platform launched around November 2025
FoundersSuman Gandham (CEO) and Vikash Srivastava (CTO)
Funding$1M seed (about ₹8.4–9.5 crore), led by Piper Serica, May 2026
Ownership (Mar 2026)Founders 72.7%, investors 20%, ESOP pool 7.3%
TeamAbout 17 employees (LinkedIn shows 23–25)
Goal$5M ARR by the end of FY27
ScaleFrom about 100,000 calls a month to millions a day in under a year (figures vary by source)

What Vobiz sells

  • Programmable telephony: SIP trunks, voice APIs, phone numbers, real-time audio streaming, WebRTC.
  • Pre-call intelligence: number health, spam-label detection. Claims about 30% less spam flagging.
  • Low latency: under 80 ms publicly; 40–50 ms in India per the demo, from fewer network hops and its own switching layer.
  • WhatsApp: became a WhatsApp Business provider in November 2026. One number can run both voice and WhatsApp. WhatsApp calling not live yet.
  • Add-ons: call recording, AI transcription, personal-data redaction.
  • Does not build AI agents. It integrates with Vapi, Retell, ElevenLabs, LiveKit, Pipecat, Bolna and Sarvam AI.

Where Vobiz sits in the value chain

Telecom carriersRaw phone network
VobizAI-ready, programmable telephony
Voice AI platformsBolna, Sarvam AI, Vapi build the agent
End businessesRazorpay, Shiprocket use it for calls

Some enterprises skip the platform layer and buy from Vobiz directly.

Customers today

SegmentShareNamed customers
Voice AI platforms and startupsAbout 70%Bolna, Sarvam AI, Smallest.ai, RevRag, Navana AI, LimeChat
EnterprisesAbout 30%Razorpay, Shiprocket

BFSI drives the most traffic, then logistics; e-commerce, healthcare and real estate are growing. Every named customer is Indian.

Business model and pricing

  • Usage-based, billed monthly. No platform fee and no charge for APIs or webhooks; similar providers charge about ₹6,000 a month.
  • Numbers (India): ₹500/month (80/79 series), ₹600 then ₹500 (140/160 series, BFSI), ₹1,000–2,000 (92 series, mobile-style, claimed 15–20% higher pickup).
  • Calls: quoted as “₹0.40 per second” in the demo; almost certainly per minute. To confirm.
  • WhatsApp: about 80 paise per marketing message and 15–20 paise per utility message (Kashyap). Vobiz’s published rate of $0.0103 per marketing message (about 90 paise) confirms it; the “₹6.50” heard in the demo was a mishearing.
  • Concurrency: 3 parallel calls free, then packs of 10.
  • Self-serve: sign up, KYC, number and first call in under 10 minutes; trial credits before KYC.
  • Sub-account model: a platform can onboard its own clients under one KYC and set them up by API. Spam complaints trace back to the parent account.

International presence

  • Numbers in 130+ countries on paper and outbound calling to 190; in the Gulf this mostly means outbound only.
  • Claims early traction in the Middle East and the US; a database lists clients in 50+ countries including the UAE (unverified).
  • Pitched to MSPs and channel partners at vCon, Atlanta, October 2026.
  • No named customer, case study or office outside India.

Key insights so far

  1. International GTM starts close to zero. First revenue will most likely come from Indian customers expanding abroad.
  2. The real buyer is the AI builder, not the enterprise.
  3. Voice AI platforms are both a channel and a battleground; Vobiz must win the telephony slot inside each one.
  4. India advantages (TRAI series, DLT, INR billing) don’t travel. Vobiz needs a new wedge abroad.
  5. The GTM must be cheap and partner-led for a 17-person team.
  6. Self-serve onboarding makes developer channels testable.
  7. The sub-account model is a strong pitch to SaaS platforms that serve many clients.
  8. Voice plus WhatsApp from one number may differentiate with marketing-heavy buyers, though the sales rep showed little WhatsApp differentiation.

Still to do in this step

Pending: confirm the rate card from Vobiz’s pricing document, break down call latency into its parts (model, platform, telephony), and interview 7–10 current Vobiz customers about why they chose Vobiz.
